sections.h2: Where does an Emmet County deed get recorded?
sections.html:
Deeds for property anywhere in Emmet County are recorded at the Register of Deeds office at 200 Division Street, Suite 150, in Petoskey, Michigan 49770. The phone number on the county page is 231-348-1761.

The office handles more than 240 kinds of documents, among them deeds, mortgages with their assignments and discharges, land contracts, leases, liens, probate orders, condominium papers and plats. It also chairs the county plat board that reviews new subdivisions.

Records reach back to 1852. Images from that year forward are on file, but the name index only runs from 1922 to the present, and older indexing is added steadily. For anything earlier, the county suggests visiting and searching the index books in person.

sections.h2: What are the recording fees in Emmet County?
sections.html:
The base fee in Emmet County is $30 to enter and record any document. The register's page sets out the rest, and it states that recording fees are taken in person by cash or check only.

Emmet County register of deeds fee schedule, from the county's fee page
ServiceFee
Entering and recording any document$30
Warranty deeds, land contracts, covenant deeds and similar$35
Document that assigns or discharges more than one instrument$3 per instrument
Certification per document$5
Tax certification, up to 5 descriptions$5
Each added description20 cents
Copies$1.00 a page in the office, $1.05 online

The $35 line covers any deed with a warrant or covenant clause, and the $5 tax certification has to be included in that payment. Mail a check made out to the Emmet County Register of Deeds if you are not coming in.

sections.h2: What does Emmet County check before it accepts a document?
sections.html:
Staff compare each filing with the recording requirements in Michigan law and send back anything that falls short. The county lists the rules on its page with statute numbers, and the practical ones are below.

  • Signatures must be original, with names typed or printed beneath them, and the notary's acknowledgment must match those names.
  • The page needs a 2.5 inch blank margin at the top of the first page and half an inch on every other side.
  • Print must be black, at least 10-point, on white paper of 20-pound weight or more, sized between 8.5 by 11 and 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • The drafter's name and address must appear on any document signed in Michigan.
  • Only the last four digits of a Social Security number may appear.
  • One instrument may evidence only one recordable event.
  • Court orders must be certified and carry the clerk's seal, and a survivorship deed needs a certified death certificate on record.

Send a self-addressed return envelope. The register generally records a document the day it arrives, holds it one day and returns it the next business day, unless a title company or lender has told the office to do something else.

sections.h2: How is transfer tax figured on an Emmet County sale?
sections.html:
Michigan charges $3.75 per $500 of value for the state tax (MCL 207.525) and 55 cents per $500 for the county tax in a county with fewer than 2,000,000 people (MCL 207.504). The register's page tells filers that the full sale price must show on the deed or in an attached valuation affidavit.

The county posts a transfer tax table, a list of exemptions and a state refund application among the downloads on its page. The statutes put the tax on the seller (MCL 207.502 and 207.523).

With the Census Bureau's 2020-2024 median value for Emmet County of $315,700, a sale lands on 632 units of $500. That produces $2,370.00 of state tax and $347.60 of county tax, a total of $2,717.60. A parent who deeds a house to a child, or a grandparent to a grandchild, is exempt from the state tax under MCL 207.526, and the exemption must be written on the instrument.

sections.h2: Why does recording order matter in Michigan?
sections.html:
Michigan follows a race-notice rule, which Emmet County's register explains in plain terms: recording a deed puts later buyers on notice, so the order in which papers are presented decides priority. First in time is first in line.

For a seller that means the deed and the buyer's mortgage should both reach the register promptly after closing. A gap lets a later filing jump ahead. Title companies know this and usually record the same day. If you are handling a private sale without one, deliver the deed yourself or use one of the e-recording services the county works with: CSC, EPN or Simplifile.

The county page carries a ROD Alert about outside companies that offer certified copies of a deed for $50 or more. Copies of land records cost as little as $1 a page at the register, and the office asks residents to call 231-348-1761 before paying a third party.

sections.h2: How can you search Emmet County records for free?
sections.html:
Emmet County offers a free online records search once you register. Searches run by liber and page, name or document type, and a preview image shows before you buy a copy at $1.05 a page by card. A companion service, Fraud Notify, emails you whenever a document is recorded in your name.

Tax information is on a separate property search on the county website, which accepts a name, address or parcel number. Anyone buying or inheriting a house in the county should check both before signing.

sections.h2: What does Emmet County look like for a house seller?
sections.html:
Emmet County sits at the top of the Lower Peninsula with Lake Michigan to the west and the Straits of Mackinac to the north. It totals 882 square miles, but only 467 are land, because Little Traverse Bay and lakes take up 47% of the area. Petoskey is the county seat and the largest city. Harbor Springs is the other city, and the villages are Alanson, Pellston and part of Mackinaw City.

The Census Bureau's 2020-2024 figures show a median owner-occupied value of $315,700, 77.0% of homes owner-occupied and 15,190 households. The county estimate for July 2025 was 33,775 people in about 22,395 housing units, and 28.5% of residents are 65 or older.

Moeller Aerospace Technology is in Harbor Springs, and Kilwins, the candy and ice cream company founded in 1947, is based in Petoskey. McLaren Northern Michigan Hospital in Petoskey employs about 950 people, and the Odawa Casino Resort in Resort Township is among the county's top attractions. Median household income is $78,112.

sections.h2: What if the house has back taxes in Emmet County?
sections.html:
Delinquent taxes are collected through the county treasurer's office, and a deed cannot be recorded without a tax certification from that office. The register accepts redemption payments from owners during the redemption period; after it ends, only the foreclosing unit can help.

Selling can resolve the debt. The closer pays the balance from proceeds, then requests the certification the register needs. Ask the county treasurer for a payoff figure before you set a closing date.

faqs.q: What is the address of the Emmet County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: 200 Division Street, Suite 150, Petoskey, MI 49770. Call 231-348-1761. Recording fees are paid in person by cash or check only.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Emmet County?
faqs.a: The base fee is $30, and warranty deeds, land contracts and other deeds with covenant language are $35. A $5 tax certification is added and must be included with the payment.

faqs.q: Does Emmet County accept electronic recording?
faqs.a: Yes. The register works with three e-recording providers: CSC, EPN and Simplifile. Contact one of them for guidance on submitting a deed electronically.

faqs.q: How far back do Emmet County records go?
faqs.a: Records start in 1852. Images are indexed from 1922 to today, and earlier indexing is ongoing, so older searches may require a visit to the index books.

faqs.q: Do I need witnesses on an Emmet County deed?
faqs.a: No. The county says documents signed in Michigan no longer need witnesses, though most require a notary acknowledgment. Check the recording requirements list for the specifics.
